about: Historical re-entry cases for forecast validation. load_replay_case forces replay=true, so a score from these rows is not a live prediction. elements is null: no public pre-decay GP/TLE was found without a Space-Track login. gp_history is authenticated and limited to one request per object per lifetime (docs/SPACETRACK_NOTES.md). CelesTrak's public GP feed does not serve these decayed epochs. No element set is invented. decay_at is the CelesTrak SATCAT DECAY_DATE stored as 00:00:00Z because that field has no time of day.

cases.name: DELTA 2 R/B
cases.elements_reason: No public GP/TLE for a pre-decay epoch. Not fabricated.
cases.finds_reason: Published accounts name Georgetown, Texas (tank) and Seguin, Texas (titanium sphere) but do not give a surveyed lat/lon.
cases.note: CelesTrak SATCAT DECAY_DATE 1997-01-22 for NORAD 23852 (1996-024B DELTA 2 R/B), queried 2026-10-25, stored as 00:00:00Z. Debris: Smithsonian Air & Space, The Things That Fell to Earth; ESA image Debris landed in Texas; SeeSat-L Feb 1997. No surveyed lat/lon, so finds is empty. Elements omitted.

cases.name: FALCON 9 R/B
cases.elements_reason: No public GP/TLE for a pre-decay epoch. Not fabricated. Aerospace.org reentry id cited by NASA ARES is 47782.
cases.finds_reason: A COPV was recovered in Grant County, Washington. The sheriff did not publish the farm coordinates (Space.com, 2021-04-03). The NASA ARES coordinate is a radar/event reference, not that find, so it is not stored as a find point.
cases.note: CelesTrak SATCAT DECAY_DATE 2021-03-26 for NORAD 47782 (2021-017BN FALCON 9 R/B), queried 2026-10-25, stored as 00:00:00Z. NASA ARES reports the reentry at 2021-03-26 04:00 UTC; that clock time is not substituted for the catalog date. COPV find location was not published. Elements omitted.
